overview: This Senate resolution celebrates the 100th anniversary of the Grand Ole Opry, the country music radio show and stage in Nashville, Tennessee. It recounts the show's history, from its 1925 start as a radio barn dance, through its years at the Ryman Auditorium, to its 1974 move to the Grand Ole Opry House, and notes that it is the longest-running radio show in U.S. history. The resolution honors the Opry's role in shaping country music and congratulates its artists and members. It is a statement of recognition and does not create any program or spend money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 7, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution fittingly honors a century-old American institution that has shaped country music and the culture of the nation.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
